p01.why: twice.h defines a non-inline function, and both units include it, so the program has two definitions of twice.

p02.why: The static data member Box::count is defined twice in one unit.

p03.why: start_of<int> is one variable in the program, so the other unit sees the 8, and start_of<long> keeps 7.

p04.why: A guard value does not change the guard, so the second inclusion adds nothing; the macro value 1 is usable in the static_assert.

p05.why: The local class only reads the value of a local constant and a non-mutable member of a local constexpr object, which is no use.

p06.why: The include guard makes the second inclusion empty.

p07.why: An inline variable is defined twice in one unit.

p08.why: Binding a reference to Limits::top uses it, and the static member has no definition outside the class.

p09.why: The enumeration Color is defined twice in one unit.

p10.why: Only one unit declares the explicit specialization; no diagnostic is required and the program accepts either result.

p11.why: pragma once after text still makes every later inclusion add nothing, including the text before it.

p12.why: "../level.h" is found relative to nested/, so it is the top-level level.h with level 1.

p13.why: Repeated declarations are not definitions, and each entity is defined once; 2+1+1 is 4.

p14.why: Binding a reference to the local constant in a local class is a use; Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts.

p15.why: Every name of the undefined entities is in an unevaluated operand or a discarded statement, so nothing is used and the program links.

p16.why: The lambda copies a whole local constexpr class object without a capture; Clang rejects, GCC and EDG accept and the program returns 0.

p17.why: rate<char> is a non-inline explicit specialization of a variable template defined in a header that two units include.

p18.why: Only one unit declares the partial specialization; no diagnostic is required and the program accepts either result.

p19.why: Reading a mutable member of a local constant is a use without a capture; Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts.

p20.why: Derived's destructor uses Base's pure destructor, which has no definition.

p21.why: The two definitions of Level differ, which needs no diagnostic; each unit uses its own enumerator values, 1 and 5, so the sum is 6.

p22.why: Members and the static data member of the class template are shared across units, with one Box<int>::made.

p23.why: The call does not use the default argument, so seed is not used and needs no definition.

p24.why: A function with internal linkage is used and not defined; Clang and GCC warn, and -Werror makes the warning an error (EDG skips the test).

p25.why: The partial specialization's member, the class specialization's member defined in one unit, and the inline explicit specializations each have one address.

p26.why: pragma once makes the second inclusion add nothing.

p27.why: Clang and GCC 16 give lower<int> and upper<int> one object and run; GCC 14 gives each unit its own object of a const or constexpr variable template, so the run returns 3.

p28.why: Comments before the guard do not stop it.

p29.why: A virtual destructor uses its class's operator delete, which is declared and not defined.

p30.why: total is defined twice in one unit.

p31.why: The static member of an explicit class specialization follows ODR-8, and the header defines it in both units.

p32.why: The delete expression uses Item's destructor, which has no definition.

p33.why: The function template specialization and its static local have one address in the program.

p35.why: Whole's default constructor uses Part's constructor, which has no definition.

p36.why: The call uses the default argument, so seed is used and has no definition.

p37.why: The include is replaced by the text 1, so main returns 1 - 1.

p38.why: Taking the function's address uses it, and it has no definition.

p39.why: The template argument uses declared_only, but every compiler links when nothing calls the function, which ODR-8 allows.

p40.why: Node's constructor can throw, so the new expression uses Node::operator delete, which has no definition.

p41.why: Text after the guard's endif is added at each inclusion, so Outside is defined twice.

p42.why: Both names appear only in sizeof, so neither is used.

p43.why: Member functions that are never used need no definition.

p45.why: The inline constexpr is one object, the plain constexpr is one per unit, and far_limit is defined once with external linkage and read at run time.

p46.why: The template argument uses a function with internal linkage that has no definition; Clang warns and -Werror rejects, GCC gives no diagnostic and runs; EDG skips.

p47.why: counter.h has no guard, so counter is defined twice in the unit.

p48.why: The only use of the undefined internal function is in an inline function nothing calls; Clang 22 and EDG reject, GCC gives no diagnostic and Clang 18 only warns, so both run.

p49.why: Nested conditionals inside the guard do not stop it; Nested's v is 4.

p50.why: Only pick(int) is selected from the overload set, so the undefined pick(double) is not used.

p51.why: The enumeration is defined the same way in both units and next_code once.

p52.why: The class templates differ, which needs no diagnostic; the program accepts either size.

p53.why: The inline variables differ, which needs no diagnostic; the program accepts either value.

p54.why: Only one unit declares the explicit specialization; no diagnostic, and the program accepts either result.

p55.why: The copy uses the copy constructor, which has no definition.

p56.why: Each prvalue initializes an object of its own type, so no copy or move constructor is used.

p57.why: pragma once makes the second inclusion add nothing.

p58.why: Every occurrence of Limits::top and width only reads a constant value, so Limits::top needs no definition; 5 + 8 is 13.

p59.why: Both units declare the explicit specialization, and one unit defines it.

p60.why: The guard skips the second inclusion, the inline variable has one address, and perimeter is defined once.

p61.why: Each `int total;` is a definition, so total is defined twice in one unit.

p62.why: The variable templates differ, which needs no diagnostic; the program accepts either value.

p63.why: factor names a different entity in each unit, so the definitions do not match; no diagnostic, and either result is accepted.

p64.why: "level.h" from nested/outer.h finds nested/level.h first, so level is 2.

p65.why: Creating a Widget uses every virtual function that is not pure, and draw has no definition.

p66.why: Destroying guard uses ~Guard, which has no definition.

p67.why: The class definitions differ, which needs no diagnostic; the program accepts either size.

p68.why: The lambdas only read values of local constants (through ?:) and of a constexpr member, and alias is a namespace-scope reference, so no capture is needed.

p69.why: The inline functions name different factor objects, so they do not match; no diagnostic, and either result is accepted.

p70.why: A function in an unnamed namespace has internal linkage and is used without a definition; the warning becomes an error under -Werror.
